claim: **Definitions.** A test, helper or fixture under `tests/` *uses SQLite* when it does any of these: names a `sqlite` URL; reads a file under `examples/sqlite-demo/`; imports or calls Python's `sqlite3` module or anything in `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite`; calls `sqllens.preflight._probe_sqlite`, or a preflight path that reaches it with a `sqlite` URL; passes `"sqlite"` as a dialect or engine value; or relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union (`load_extension`, or a `sqlite_` or `pragma_` name, a CTE or table so named included). A case relies on such an entry when it runs under a `None` or unknown dialect and its outcome comes from that entry. It also relies on one when, under any dialect, its outcome differs from the `None`-dialect outcome only because the entry is in the union. An example is a `sqlite_`-prefixed data table under dialect `mysql` that proves the configured dialect arrives, as in the MySQL row #382 gave `test_with_widgets_hides_introspection_result_under_configured_dialect`. Naming ChromaDB's `chroma.sqlite3` file is not a use. A use is *SQLite-only* when the behaviour it asserts exists only for SQLite. That covers at minimum: the `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite` package, `sqlite_path_from_url` and `_readonly_uri`; the SQLite preflight probe; a `sqlite`-keyed entry of a per-dialect table in `src/sqllens/safety/` or in the system prompt (for example `sqlite_master`, `pragma_*` names, `load_extension`); `sqllens init`'s SQLite template; `claude-desktop install`'s SQLite file-stem naming; a case that relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union; and a `sqlite` case whose expected outcome differs from the same test's `mysql` case with the same other inputs. A use whose classification is unclear counts as SQLite-only, and its test also gets a MySQL version. A `sqlite` URL used only as the non-MySQL input that a MySQL-only check refuses (`tests/unit/test_rule_set_file.py::test_non_mysql_url_is_refused`, `tests/unit/test_cli_rule_sets.py::test_validate_refuses_a_non_mysql_url`) is engine-neutral where another non-MySQL scheme can reach that check: its replacement passes one, for example `postgresql://u@db.invalid/shop`, straight to `load_rule_sets`, and asserts the same refusal. Where config load refuses every other scheme before the check runs (`sqllens validate`), the use is SQLite-only, and its map row says no MySQL counterpart exists because config load accepts only MySQL and SQLite URLs. Every other use is *engine-neutral*. After the change, every use of SQLite under `tests/` is SQLite-only.
verify_hint: Check `test_non_mysql_url_is_refused` and the `_load` helper in test_rule_set_file.py.

claim: For the dialect cases of every test: - A `sqlite` case with the same other inputs and the same expected outcome as an existing `mysql` case of that test is removed. - An engine-neutral case (as the first criterion defines it) that ran only under `sqlite` runs under `mysql`. Its outcome under `mysql` can differ from its SQLite expectation for two excused causes, and in both the SQLite case stays as SQLite-only: - a `mysql`- or `sqlite`-keyed entry or branch of a per-dialect table or dialect check in `src/`. The MySQL case asserts the code's MySQL outcome. - sqlglot's `mysql` grammar reading the same text differently (for example, `#` starts a comment and a double-quoted name is a string, only under `mysql`). The MySQL case is the input written in MySQL syntax with the same meaning (for example, backticks for a quoted name, or an unparseable statement with no `#`), and it asserts the SQLite case's outcome. An existing `mysql` case of the test that already is that input stands in for it. Any other difference, or one whose cause is unclear, is a defect handled as the last criterion states. - The default `dialect` of `_assert_filtered_and_readonly` in `tests/unit/test_safety_rls.py` is `"mysql"`. - Every `None`-dialect and unknown-dialect case that exists at the merge base still exists. - Each such case that relies on a SQLite entry of the fallback union (a SQLite-only case, as the first criterion defines it) has a counterpart in the same test, under each of the dialect values that case uses. The same applies to each case of any dialect that relies on such an entry. The counterpart relies only on a MySQL entry or on MySQL-only syntax (for example `load_file`, `sleep`, a table in the `mysql`, `sys` or `performance_schema` schema, or a statement only the `mysql` dialect reads, such as `# note\nSHOW TABLES`). It asserts the same outcome as the SQLite case. If the code gives the MySQL entry a different outcome, the difference is handled as the last criterion states. The exception is a case whose outcome no MySQL entry or syntax can produce; for example, a CTE-shadowing case needs a name prefix, and MySQL's catalog entry has none. Its map row states that no MySQL counterpart exists and why. For `test_with_widgets_hides_introspection_result_under_configured_dialect`, the counterpart row's catalog statement is one only the `mysql` dialect classifies as introspection (for example `# note\nSHOW TABLES`), so the test fails when the configured dialect does not reach the formatter.

A test or case is named by its node ID, and a helper or fixture by `path::name`. Each row gives the node ID or IDs of its MySQL replacement (the same test when only its URL or dialect changed), or `SQLite-only, deleted in #383`. A row for a test whose classification was unclear gives both. A SQLite-only row with no possible MySQL counterpart says so and why. Tests in one file with the same outcome may share a row that names them.

claim: Line coverage does not drop against the merge base. Instrument: coverage.py, installed with `pip install coverage` for the measurement only, `python -m coverage run -m pytest -q`, then `python -m coverage json`, comparing each file's `executed_lines` under all of `src/sqllens/`. Every line that the merge base's default run executes is also executed by this branch's default run with the map's `SQLite-only` tests deselected. Lines are matched through the PR's diff of `src/`: a line the diff deletes needs no match, and every line the diff adds that coverage.py reports as a statement (in `executed_lines` or `missing_lines`) is executed. The one exception is a line that no non-SQLite input can execute. It is defined by where the code is, not by which tests ran: a line in `sqllens.agent.integrations.sqlite` or `sqllens.preflight._probe_sqlite`, or a line inside a branch whose condition holds only for the `sqlite` dialect, a URL whose scheme starts with `sqlite`, or a SQLite database file, or a line in a function whose every caller is such a line (for example `sqllens.safety.relations._sqlite_kind`). When it is unclear whether a line is such a line, a MySQL test executes it. The PR body states the merge-base SHA compared against, and lists each excepted line as `path:line` or a line range with the SQLite-only condition that guards it.

claim: Each SQLite-only test (as the first criterion defines it) still runs and passes in the default run. The change leaves every file under `src/` unchanged except for the fix to a security defect that a new or moved test exposes. The list of security defects is closed. A security defect is a defect in the code of one of these guards that lets it be bypassed or weakened under the `mysql` dialect or a MySQL URL: the read-only guard (`ReadOnlyGuardRunner`, `assert_select_only`), the function denylist, row-level security (`RlsGuardRunner`, `apply_rls`) and its relation check (`verify_base_tables`), result masking (`ResultMaskingRunner`), the row cap (`RowCapRunner` and the runner's `fetchmany` cap), the whole-row guard (`WholeRowSelectGuardRunner`), the per-role rule-set guard (`RuleSetGuardRunner`, `apply_rule_set`: its table and column limits, catalog-read rewrite and row rules) and refusal redaction (`RefusalRedactingRunner`). A defect for which it is unclear whether it lies in one of these guards' code, or whether it bypasses or weakens one, counts as a security defect. Any other defect takes the ordinary route. That includes defects clearly in the MySQL session's read-only setting (`SET SESSION TRANSACTION READ ONLY`) or statement timeout (`MAX_EXECUTION_TIME`), or in the `None`/unknown-dialect fallback. A security defect is fixed in this PR, never deferred, its exposing test passes unmarked, and no public issue is filed for it. This is the maintainer's chosen route for this issue, an exception to `SECURITY.md`'s private-report route. Any other defect a new or moved test exposes in shipped code is named in the PR body by its own issue number. Its exposing test is marked `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, raises=<the exception the defect produces>)` with a reason naming that issue.
